levels.name: First Bloom
levels.hint: Something bloomed from the stone down in the chasm. Plant on the stone, jump back up, Grow. The bloom is solid ground. Mind the green pool after it.
levels.tip: Two generations reach two cells each way: a bloom is five wide, and it began in its middle. Growth takes whatever stands inside it: be back on the rock before you grow.
levels.intro: You wake at the edge of a chasm with a lantern in your hand, and the lantern has a voice. Across the chasm, the faint outline of something that once grew.
levels.outro: The ground remembers. Where you planted the seed, the bloom grew back, and it holds your weight.
levels.says: wake|Awake. Good. I am the light; you are the legs. Down there is what is left of a bloom.||plant|A seed. Now step away from it. Growth does not care what it grows through.||grow|Watch the colours. Gold is right. Red is a guess.||found|Exact. The door felt it open. Walk.||die|The dark keeps what it takes. Not you, not yet.

levels.name: Fused Bloom
levels.hint: Two seeds lie on the road, on the ledges. The outline in the trench is one slab, but no single bloom is that wide. Two stones, close together, grew into each other.
levels.tip: A bloom is five wide. An eight-wide slab is two blooms three apart: the stones are two in from the left edge and two in from the right. Plant both, get clear, grow.
levels.intro: Two beginnings so close that their blooms fused. The road here has learned to bite: green pools, spikes, an ember with a short leash.
levels.outro: Two seeds, one slab. Nothing that grows keeps to itself.
levels.says: wake|The pool ahead is not water. Jump it.||seed|A seed. There will be two; this shape needed two.||plant|One seed in. The other goes three cells from it, or the slab comes out wrong.||grow|Both at once. If it is red at either end, one of them is off by one.||found|Fused. Two blooms, one ground. Up you go.||die|Again. Slower, this time.

levels.name: Three Sparks
levels.hint: A new law: born beside exactly one living neighbour, nothing survives. A spark leaves a ring. Three sparks left this, and where two rings would share a wall, nothing was born. Three seeds: one behind you, one up the tower, one down the pit.
levels.tip: A ring is three wide with the spark dead in its middle. Two sparks two apart share a wall cell that gets two neighbours and stays dark: that is the gap. Read the gaps for the spacing.
levels.intro: Here nothing lived past its first breath. Three sparks, three rings, grown into one another. The seeds were scattered: back, up, and down.
levels.outro: Three sparks, one ring. Where they touched, they cancelled. Even light has edges.
levels.says: wake|Three seeds this time. One of them is behind you. Nobody looks behind them.||seed|One. Keep counting.||plant|Two apart makes a shared wall and a gap. Three apart makes a bridge.||grow|One generation. Blink and it is done.||found|Three rings, exact. The ring is ground. Climb.||die|That was the wrong way to learn it, but you learned it.

levels.name: Shadow
levels.hint: Here nothing dies, and a cell is born only beside exactly one neighbour, so growth is thin and easily blocked. A rock post stands in this coral. Growth is light: the post cast a shadow, and the shadow falls away from the stone.
levels.tip: Cells that could not be born because the post stood between them and the stone are missing on the post's far side. The stone is on the near side, on the floor, two from the post.
levels.intro: Everything ever born here is still here, thin as coral. And a post of rock stood in the middle of it while it grew.
levels.outro: The coral remembers the post as a shadow. So does the ground remember you.
levels.says: wake|The blocks up this shaft do not like being stood on. Keep moving.||plant|Beside the post, on its lit side. If you are wrong the shadow will fall the wrong way.||grow|Five generations. Watch how it goes around the post.||found|The shadow fell where it should. Up the coral, then.||die|Everything that grew here died once too.

levels.name: Cut Echo
levels.hint: A stranger law: a cell lives when its neighbour count is odd. Each echo grew three generations from a trench floor and the cliff cut off whatever reached it. Two seeds lie on the way. The echo's top is the only way up each cliff.
levels.tip: Three generations reach three cells out: the echo's far column stands three from the stone. Count from the open side, on the floor. It is not in the middle of what you can see.
levels.intro: Deeper in, the law is stranger. What lived here echoed, and the echoes climbed the cliffs before the rock cut them short.
levels.outro: An echo is the shape of its source, repeated and thinned. You are learning the grammar.
levels.says: wake|Vents ahead. They breathe fire on a count. Learn the count.||plant|The cliff ate half of it. Count from the half you can see.||grow|Odd neighbours live. Even ones do not. Watch it thin.||found|Cut short, and still enough. Up.||die|I have the light. You have the legs. Try once more.

levels.name: Bent Echo
levels.hint: The lake is crossed on stones that do not hold. Beyond it an echo grew against a post of rock and bent around it. The stone sits in the crook, against the post. The boulder before the echo is your step onto it.
levels.tip: An echo in the open is symmetric. This one is heavy on one side and empty on the other: the post blocked it. The stone is on the floor, right beside the post, on the heavy side.
levels.intro: A lake that eats lanterns, crossed on stones that fall. And past it an echo that grew crooked, because something stood in its way.
levels.outro: Bent, not broken. The post is still there. So is the shape.
levels.says: wake|The stones in the lake fall a heartbeat after you land. Do not admire the view.||plant|Against the post. Growth leans away from what blocks it.||grow|Three generations, one of them crooked.||found|Crooked and exact. Up the echo.||die|The lake does not give things back.

levels.name: Quench
levels.hint: An ember paces the low cave. The stone is on its floor, by the far wall, and the wall cut the bloom short. Drop in when the ember is far, plant, climb the boulder, Grow: a bloom puts out any ember it reaches, and its top is the way on.
levels.tip: Growth takes whatever stands inside it, ember or wanderer. Three generations make a bloom seven wide; the wall cut this one to five. Count three in from the open edge: the stone is right against the wall.
levels.intro: Something still burns down there, in a cave too low to stand tall in. Embers hate what grows. Plant beneath one and see.
levels.outro: The ember went out in the bloom. What grows again does not burn.
levels.says: wake|Spikes on the road. They do not move. That is their whole trick.||plant|Now out, before it notices you. It is coming back.||grow|Three generations. If the ember is inside them, it is over for it.||found|Out. What grows again does not burn. The bridge past the vents does not hold; cross it running.||die|The ember is faster than it looks. So are you, when you want to be.

levels.name: Ashfall
levels.hint: Climb the ledges; a seed lies on one, some of them fall, and an ember rises and falls between them. Above: a shelf with vents, a pit with a stone and an ember, a second seed, a second pit. Two blooms, one after the other, up to the door.
levels.tip: Each pit's bloom was cut by the pit's far wall: the stone is one cell from that wall, not in the middle. Grow the first, fetch the second seed, plant, climb out, rewind, grow both from the ledge.
levels.intro: The cave climbs, and what is under it is green and does not forgive. Ledge by ledge, with an ember rising and falling in the dark between them.
levels.outro: You climbed through the dark and grew a stair at the top of it. The way down is behind you now.
levels.says: wake|Look down. Now do not look down again.||seed|One seed. There is another, higher.||plant|Against the wall of the pit. The wall will take a third of the bloom; the rest is yours.||grow|Three generations. Stand on the rim, not in it.||found|Stair by stair. The door is at the top.||die|Falling is quick. Climbing is not. Climb.

levels.name: Two Echoes
levels.hint: Two seeds hide in this warren: one at the end of the low tunnel, one on the shelf above it, reached by the falling blocks. In the trench, two echoes crossed and cancelled where they met: a cell with an even count stays dark. Find where each began.
levels.tip: The shape is symmetric, but nothing began at its centre: that is where the two echoes cancelled. The stones are two cells apart on the floor, one either side of the middle, each right beside a lone floor cell.
levels.intro: Two origins, close enough to touch. Their echoes crossed, and where they crossed they cancelled, and the shape they left has a hole where you would look first.
levels.outro: Two beginnings, one shape. Nothing that grows keeps its own edges.
levels.says: wake|Two seeds, and this place hides both. Low first, then high.||seed|One. The other is above your head somewhere.||plant|Two apart. Any closer and they are one echo; any further and they stop cancelling.||grow|Watch the middle stay dark. That is two things agreeing to disappear.||found|Cancelled and exact. Up the echo, past the vents.||die|The vent counts to three and breathes. Count with it.

levels.name: Origin
levels.hint: The seed lies in the pit between the spikes, where an ember paces. The stone stands on the pillar's top, behind the low post and against the wall. The ladder climbs past a rising ember. Plant, come back down, Grow, climb the bloom over the wall to the high road.
levels.tip: Four generations reach four cells out. The wall cut this bloom: count four back from its open edge and you have the stone. The post inside it only bends the top. Wait on the ladder, at least five cells from the stone, before you grow.
levels.intro: The highest stone in the deepest cave. You have found where every ruin began. This is where you began: a seed in a pit, a stone on a pillar against a wall, and an ember rising and falling between them.
levels.outro: The last bloom grew from the highest point, and you climbed it into the light. You were its seed.
levels.says: wake|Everything this cave knows how to do, it will do to you between here and the pillar. I have seen it all. You will see it once.||seed|The last seed. Do not fall on the way up; I cannot carry you.||plant|Against the wall, behind the post. Now down the ladder, well below it, before you grow.||grow|Four generations. It will be a mountain.||found|There. That is where you began. Climb it into the light; I will come with you.||die|Not here. Not this close.
